Does this inspire you and feel like a fit? Then we would love to have you join us!

**The Role

**The Senior Manager, Clinical Programming is responsible for the establishment, governance, and integrity of Study Data Tabulation Model (SDTM) standards, perform sponsor oversight of relevant programming activities on the Biometrics vendor, ensure the quality and consistency of data standards to support the portfolio towards the ultimate objective of data quality and consistency across programs and systems.

**Responsibilities

**

• Develops and implements company Study Data Tabulation Model (SDTM) standards that support the scientific need of a study/program while ensuring quality, consistency and compliance to CDISC standards and other industry standards that supports the exchange of data, reporting, and analysis.

• Ensures alignment of SDTM standards with data collection standards and relevant company tools/system requirements by reviewing study eCRFs, supporting creation of external data collection standards, and providing SDTM mapping guidance

• Serves as a subject matter expert on all aspects of standards development that includes industry standards (CDISC), regulations, and processes

• Ensures study or portfolio-level SDTM datasets are in compliance with CDISC and regulatory submission requirements, reviews study submission data packages to ensure quality and integrity

• Directly supports knowledge development of others as a subject matter expert on data standards, reporting and analysis standards, change control management and related tools/applications

• Creates quality control processes, metrics and other measures to ensure compliance with standards

• Ensures work carried out in accordance with applicable SOP’s and working practices, as well as global agency regulations/guidance’s

• Creates any needed documentation and training for standard processes, change control management and tools

• Responsible for defining standards specifications working closely with implementation support teams (database set-up, completion guidelines, CRF designers, procedures, algorithm specifications and reporting requirements)

• Facilitates a culture of continuous process improvement and a high level of customer service by maintaining and improving the standards processes associated with standards creation, maintenance, decision-making and implementation

• Working with Digital Solutions and IT, support the implementation of future strategies and technology-enabled processes and tools for clinical trials standards, change control management and the exchange of standards information to internal downstream consumers and externally consumers

• Serves as a liaison between Clinical Programming and External Data Management to ensure data standardization alignment and proactively resolve external data issues that impact SDTM deliverables.

**Requirements

**

• Bachelor’s degree in Statistics, Computer Science, Life Sciences. Master’s degree in Statistics, Computer Science, Life Sciences preferred

• At least 6-8 years relevant experience in a pharmaceutical, biotech, CRO or Regulatory Agency

• Proficient in SAS programming, 6-8 years experience.

• Practical knowledge and experience using R to support clinical trial preferred

• Demonstrated knowledge of clinical research, metadata management, industry standards (CDISC), FDA & ICH, GCP, and related regulatory requirements

• Demonstrated experience managing multiple tasks, complex projects and working with cross functional teams delivering to project and portfolio timelines and metrics

• Strong verbal and written communication skills; independent and effective working in a multi-study, multi-disciplinary atmosphere in a matrix environment

• Experience in clinical data management and/or trial management experience with technical expertise in standards management and implementation is preferred.

jobs.occupation: Kok med speciale i kinesisk gastronomi søges til YoYo Restaurantionsselskab ApS i Hundested & Chef Specializing in Chinese Cuisine Wanted at YoYo Restaurantionsselskab ApS in Hundested
jobs.description:
Vi søger 1 kok til vores restaurant i Hundested.

Har du passion for autentisk kinesisk madlavning, gode råvarer og kulinariske oplevelser? Har du samtidig erfaring med sushi, er det en ekstra fordel. Så er du måske vores nye kollega!

YoYo Restaurantionsselskab ApS er en kinesisk restaurant beliggende på Nørregade 29A, 3390 Hundested. Vi lægger vægt på traditionelle kinesiske retter, autentiske smagsoplevelser og god service i hyggelige omgivelser. Vores køkken kombinerer kinesiske madtraditioner med et udvalg af andre asiatiske retter, herunder sushi.

Vi søger en dygtig og engageret kok med erfaring inden for kinesisk gastronomi, som kan bidrage til den daglige drift og den fortsatte udvikling af vores køkken. Du bliver en del af et team, hvor kvalitet, samarbejde og respekt for asiatiske madtraditioner er i centrum.

Dine primære arbejdsopgaver

• 
Tilberede autentiske kinesiske retter med fokus på kvalitet, smag og præsentation.

• 
Klargøre råvarer samt fremstille saucer, marinader og andre centrale elementer i det kinesiske køkken.

• 
Medvirke til udvikling og tilpasning af menuer og nye retter.

• 
Efter behov bidrage til tilberedning og anretning af sushi og andre asiatisk inspirerede retter.

• 
Sikre korrekt håndtering og opbevaring af råvarer samt overholdelse af gældende hygiejne- og fødevaresikkerhedsregler.

• 
Bidrage til en effektiv og velfungerende daglig drift i samarbejde med resten af køkkenteamet.

Vi forventer, at du

• 
Har praktisk erfaring med kinesisk gastronomi og gerne kendskab til forskellige regionale kinesiske køkkentraditioner.

• 
Har en god forståelse for råvarer, traditionelle tilberedningsteknikker og sammensætning af smage.

• 
Gerne har erfaring med tilberedning af sushi, herunder håndtering af råvarer, tilberedning af sushiris, rulleteknikker og anretning. Erfaring med sushi er en fordel, men ikke et krav.

• 
Kan arbejde selvstændigt, struktureret og effektivt – også i travle perioder.

• 
Har sans for detaljer, kvalitet og præsentation af maden.

• 
Er mødestabil, ansvarsbevidst og har gode samarbejdsevner.

• 
Har lyst til at bidrage aktivt til restaurantens udvikling og fastholde en høj gastronomisk standard.

• 
Gerne taler kinesisk, da det kan være en fordel i den daglige kommunikation og i arbejdet med traditionelle kinesiske opskrifter. Det er dog ikke et krav.

Vi tilbyder

• 
En spændende stilling i en veletableret kinesisk restaurant med stærk lokal forankring.

• 
Mulighed for faglig udvikling og indflydelse på køkkenets retter og menuer.

• 
Mulighed for at arbejde med både traditionelle kinesiske retter og andre asiatiske specialiteter, herunder sushi.

• 
Et uformelt og samarbejdsorienteret arbejdsmiljø med plads til engagement og faglig stolthed.

• 
En varieret arbejdsdag med engagerede kollegaer.

• 
Løn- og ansættelsesvilkår efter kvalifikationer og nærmere aftale.

Om os

Hos YoYo Restaurantionsselskab ApS handler mad om mere end blot at stille sulten. Vi ønsker at skabe autentiske madoplevelser, hvor traditionelle tilberedningsmetoder, velafbalancerede smage og gode råvarer går hånd i hånd.

Fra duften af frisklavede wokretter til omhyggeligt tilberedt sushi stræber vi efter at tilbyde vores gæster en varieret og mindeværdig asiatisk madoplevelse i hjertet af Hundested.

Lyder stillingen som noget for dig? Så hører vi gerne fra dig.

Send din ansøgning og dit CV til restauranten, eller kontakt os for yderligere oplysninger om stillingen.

Siteimprove helps organisations make their digital content accessible to everyone. Our accessibility products scan entire web estates and document libraries, find the barriers that stop people using them, and increasingly fix those barriers automatically. The work is measured in public: our customers are universities, health systems, government agencies and Fortune 500 companies who have legal deadlines to meet and auditors to satisfy.

We are looking for a Senior Engineering Manager to lead one of our two accessibility product teams. You will own the delivery, quality and technical direction of a cross-functional team of engineers working alongside a Product Manager and a Designer, and you will be accountable for what that team ships and for how the people in it grow.

This role sits at a genuine inflection point. We are moving from finding accessibility problems to explaining and fixing them, and we are rebuilding how we develop software around AI agents that write, test and review code under human direction. We need a leader who is credible in the code, fluent in modern AI-assisted development, and able to coach a team through that change without trading away quality or the well-being of the people doing the work.

What we will be doing

• 
Own delivery for your team. Turn a product roadmap into a sequenced, realistic plan, keep commitments honest, and be the person who says early and clearly when something will not land.

• 
Lead the people. Hold regular one-to-ones, give direct and useful feedback, run performance and growth conversations, and build a team where engineers at different levels can do their best work. Recruit, onboard and retain.

• 
Stay hands-on enough to be credible. Read and review code and designs, take part in architectural decisions, and pair with engineers when it helps. You are not expected to carry a full delivery load, but you are expected to understand the system well enough to challenge a design and to know when an estimate is wrong.

• 
Coach the team in AI-assisted development. Raise the whole team's effectiveness with AI tooling: how to decompose a problem so an agent can take it, how to write a prompt and a specification that produce reviewable work, and how to review agent-generated code properly rather than approving it on sight.

• 
Set the standards for how AI-generated work is accepted. Define with your engineers how such work is reviewed, tested, secured and documented before it merges, and hold the line that a human is always accountable for what ships.

• 
Partner with Product and Design as equals. Work with your Product Manager on outcomes, scope and sequencing, and make the technical trade-offs visible so the three of you decide together.

• 
Work across teams. Depend on and contribute to Platform, AI and other product teams. Much of what your team needs will be built elsewhere, and much of what it builds will be consumed elsewhere.

• 
Protect engineering health. Hold a deliberate balance between roadmap delivery, compliance obligations, customer-reported defects and technical debt, and make that balance explicit rather than letting it be decided by whatever is loudest.

• 
Own quality and operational responsibility. Testing, accessibility conformance of our own products, security and vulnerability remediation, incident response and the reliability of what your team runs in production.

• 
Adjust your working hours to overlap with the United States. This role reports to a manager on the US Pacific coast and partners with colleagues across the US. You will regularly take meetings in the late afternoon or early evening Central European Time, and we will protect the rest of your week in return.

• 
Travel may be required; a valid passport is required

• 
Perform other duties as assigned

What we will require of you

• 
Engineering management experience. Several years leading software engineering teams as their direct manager, including hiring, performance management and developing engineers at more than one level. You have owned delivery for a team over a sustained period, not just a project.

• 
A real software engineering background. You have built and shipped production software yourself and can still read a pull request, follow a design discussion and form your own view. We will talk about systems you have built.

• 
Depth in at least one of our core languages, and comfort across the rest. Our services are written mainly in C# and .NET, TypeScript and JavaScript, Go, Rust and Python. You do not need all of them; you do need to be genuinely strong in one and unafraid of the others.

• 
Modern cloud and delivery practice. AWS, containers and Kubernetes, infrastructure as code, continuous integration and deployment pipelines, observability and on-call practice.

• 
Practical use of AI in the software lifecycle. You have personally used AI coding assistants and agents on real work, you know where they help and where they mislead, and you have opinions about how their output should be reviewed. Experience helping other engineers adopt them is what sets this role apart.

• 
Strong partnership with Product. A track record of working with Product Managers and Designers as a peer, shaping scope rather than receiving it.

• 
Clear written and spoken English, and the ability to explain a technical trade-off to a non-technical audience.

• 
Willingness to work a shifted day. Regular overlap with US Pacific time, and occasional travel.

What we will love about you

• 
Digital accessibility knowledge. Familiarity with WCAG, assistive technology, or the accessibility conformance and reporting that regulated customers require. If you do not have it, you must be willing to learn it properly — it is the product.

• 
Experience in a compliance or regulated environment, such as FedRAMP, SOC 2, ISO 27001 or a public-sector authorisation, and comfort working inside an audited change process.

• 
Open-source stewardship. We build and maintain an open-source accessibility rules engine, and experience running a public project and its community is valuable.

Large-scale data or crawling systems, document processing, or machine learning applied to content analysis.

• 
Experience leading a distributed or multi-site team, including working effectively with contractors and vendor partners.

• 
Having introduced AI-assisted development to an organisation, including the governance, measurement and change management that goes with it.

• 
Danish language skills are a nice-to-have and are not required; our working language is English.

If you’re energized by solving complex problems, working cross-functionally, and contributing to a product with real-world impact, we’d love to connect.

jobs.description:
The Center for Quantitative Genetics and Genomics (QGG) at Aarhus University, Denmark, invites applications for a two-year postdoctoral position in plant regulatory genomics and artificial intelligence, starting 1 April 2027.

You will design new sequence-to-expression deep learning models that predict gene expression from DNA sequence in plants, using new experimental datasets generated in the project. The position includes a 6- to 12-month research stay at Cold Spring Harbor Laboratory (CSHL), USA, combining plant genomics expertise at Aarhus with AI expertise at CSHL.

This is an opportunity to advance the state of the art in AI for plant biology while working across two leading research environments. For more information, feel free to reach out to Guillaume Ramstein (QGG) and Peter Koo (CSHL).

Expected start date and duration of employment

This is a 2-year position from April 1st 2027, or as soon as possible.

Job description

You will advance the field of artificial intelligence applied to regulatory genomics, as part of the GRASP project funded by the Independent Research Fund Denmark. In this project, you will leverage new training sets, build novel deep learning architectures and define dedicated learning objectives, to learn the effects of genetic variants on gene expression.

The position will focus on data science and genomics in a model plant species, Brachypodium distachyon. You will work at the cutting edge of AI in biology and propose new solutions to predict the effects of regulatory variants in plant genomes, which remains an open research problem in plant genomics. 

These activities will be carried out in close collaboration with the Koo lab, a leading group in AI and regulatory genomics at Cold Spring Harbor Laboratory (CSHL), USA. As part of this collaboration, the position will include a 6- to 12-month research stay in the Koo lab.

Your profile

Applicants should hold a PhD in computer science, bioinformatics, or a related field, or expect to complete it before the start date. They should have research experience in deep learning.

Applicants are expected to have published in international peer-reviewed journals, preferably on topics related to AI and genomics. Experience in developing new deep learning techniques (model architectures or learning objectives) is especially relevant to this position. 

Good communication skills in English are required, as well as the ability to work in an interdisciplinary team of AI experts, computational geneticists, and plant biologists.

Who we are

The Center for Quantitative Genetics and Genomics (QGG) is a major center for research and education in quantitative genetics and genomics at Aarhus University (http://www.qgg.au.dk/en). We conduct basic and applied research in animal, plant, and human genetics. Our focus areas include quantitative genetics, artificial intelligence applied to agriculture and medicine, population genetics, and integrative genomics. Research within QGG is characterized by a very close synergy between method development and application on practical problems across species, in collaboration with industry partners. QGG is an international research center with about 70 employees and visiting researchers from over 15 nations. QGG works in teams and strives for an excellent working environment, in which we value self-leadership, open communication, and commitment to diversity and inclusion.

What we offer

The succesful candidate will be offered:

• A 6- to 12-month research stay in the Koo lab at Cold Spring Harbor Laboratory (CSHL), USA, providing international experience and the opportunity to work across two leading labs in plant genomics and AI.
• Computational ressources, including the GenomeDK high-performance computing cluster, with growing capabilities such as high-memory nodes and state-of-the-art GPUs.
• An interdisciplinary interdisciplinary environment, in which the candidate will be able to exchange across research fields (machine learning, bioinformatics, biology, and quantitative genetics) and applications (plant biology, agriculture, and biomedicine).
• A research environment characterized by collaboration, professionalism, commitment to diversity and inclusion, and success in mentoring and supervision.
• A healthy work-life balance.
Place of work and area of employment

The primary place of work is C. F. Møllers Allé 3, 8000, Aarhus (Denmark), and the area of employment is Aarhus University with related departments.

The position will also include a 6- to 12-month research stay at 1 Bungtown Rd, Cold Spring Harbor, NY 11724, United States. The time and duration of the research stay may be negotiated with the supervisors Guillaume Ramstein and Peter Koo.

Contact information

For further information, please contact:

• Tenure-Track Assistant Professor Guillaume Ramstein, +45 42 52 12 66, ramstein@qgg.au.dk
• Associate Professor Peter Koo, +1 516 367 5520, koo@cshl.edu
Deadline

Applications must be received no later than November 20th, 2026.

Om Aarhus Universitet

Aarhus Universitet er et fagligt bredt og forskningsintensivt universitet med høj kvalitet i uddannelse og forskning, og et stærkt engagement i samfundsudviklingen nationalt og globalt. Universitetet tilbyder et inspirerende uddannelses- og forskningsmiljø for 37.500 studerende og 9.000 medarbejdere med en årlig omsætning på 8,9 mia. kr. Læs mere på www.au.dk

jobs.description:
Are you interested in extracellular vesicles from plants and their potential accumulation of unwanted compounds and are you willing to challenge conventional thinking? Then the Department of FOOD Science invites you to apply for a 2-year Post Doc position, funded under the Villum Experiment program.

Expected start date and duration of employment
This is a 2–year position from 1 January 2027, or as soon possible thereafter. 

Job description
The position will focus on the isolation and characterization of extracellular vesicles from plants and understanding their cargo in relation to abiotic conditions.

The Post Doc is expected to independently take part in cultivation of plants, optimizing methods for extraction of extracellular vesicles and development of targeted methods for assessing specific compounds. 

The Post Doc will likewise also be responsible for setting up and running bioactivity assays using mammalian cell-lines.

Your profile
Applicants should hold a PhD in biology, biochemistry, molecular biology, toxicology or similar.

The preferred candidate has documented hands-on experience with extracellular vesicle isolation and characterization. Likewise hands-on experience with culturing of mammalian cells and various molecular techniques like qPCR, miRNA mapping and LC-MS, is considered positive.

Strong collaborative skills, including experience working in interdisciplinary environments, are essential. We also value creative thinking, personal drive, and excellent communication skills.

Who we are
The Department of Food Science is part of the Faculty of Technical Sciences, Aarhus University and includes research within the areas Food Chemistry and Technology, Food Quality, Food Metabolomics and proteomics, Sensory Science, Biofunctional Food, Systems Biology, and Plant Production. 

The Department currently employs ca. 145 full-time staff, including 31 senior academic staff, ca. 60 PhD students and Postdocs, and ca. 45 technical and administrative staff. In addition, there are ca. 45 Bachelor and Master thesis students and ca. 10 visiting students and staff, who together contribute to an international research environment where English is the preferred language in the laboratory, at meetings and at seminars.

The Department works in teams and therefore self-leadership, clear and open communication, success in mentoring, supervising and teaching are important qualities needed to be successful in the Department. In addition, the Department has a strong culture that is based on openness, equality, consultation, inclusion and contributing to the Department strategy and working environment are viewed as important.
Aarhus University Food Science: Pioneering Research Partnerships

What we offer 
The candidate will join the multidisciplinary research environment at AU FOOD, with activities spanning the entire food value chain from field to fork. The department provides access to state-of-the-art facilities for plant cultivation under controlled conditions, advanced instrumentation for biomolecular characterization, and two fully equipped cell culture laboratories.

The candidate will join an international and multicultural workplace where English is the primary working language. The department also offers a variety of social activities that contribute to a welcoming and inclusive environment.

Place of work and area of employment 
The place of work is Agro Food Park 48, 8200 Aarhus N, and the area of employment is Aarhus University with related departments. 

Contact information
For further information, please contact: Associated Professor, Martin Krøyer Rasmussen, +452216 9390, martink.rasmussen@food.au.dk.

Deadline
Applications must be received no later than 29 October 2026. 

Application procedure
Shortlisting is used. This means that after the deadline for applications – and with the assistance from the assessment committee chairman, and the appointment committee if necessary, – the head of department selects the candidates to be evaluated. All applicants will be notified whether or not their applications have been sent to an expert assessment committee for evaluation. **About Us

nShift is the leading global provider of cloud delivery management solutions (SaaS), we enable the frictionless shipment and return of almost one billion shipments across 190 countries each year. We are headquartered in London and Oslo and have over 500 employees across offices in Sweden, Finland, Norway, Denmark, the United Kingdom, Poland, the Netherlands, Belgium, and Romania.

Our software is used by many of the world leading e-commerce, retail, manufacturing, and 3PL shippers due to us having over 1000 carriers integrated into our platform, nearly 3 times more than our competitors!

If you buy goods online, there is a strong chance that nShift has powered that delivery, so come and join us as we shape the future of shipping, one frictionless journey at a time.

**About You

**You think like a product manager and work like a data scientist. You have shipped ML-powered products to real customers and can point to the decisions you made, not just the ones made around you. Messy data, ambiguous model outputs, and stakeholders who don't yet see why the data matters are familiar territory.

You think in terms of compounding: how every data point collected today improves predictions tomorrow, and how that improvement builds a position competitors cannot close. Data insights is nShift's path from a tool company to an intelligence platform, and that scope motivates you rather than overwhelming you.

You are as comfortable in a Jupyter notebook as in a leadership meeting, and you know when each is needed.

**Purpose of role

**The mission is to define what nShift builds with that data, validate it before engineering commits, and ship intelligence products that help shippers make better decisions. A shipper asking "how can I improve my delivery experience" should get an answer powered by the full network, not just their own history. Done well, that becomes a compounding intelligence layer: every data point collected today improves suggestions tomorrow, and the improvement creates a position no competitor can close.

The intelligence layer draws from two sources. Structured operational data, such as shipment telemetry and carrier performance, feeds statistical models and predictions. Qualitative data, such as customer support interactions, delivery exception messages, and community feedback, carries signal that numbers alone cannot surface. LLMs make that signal extractable and usable at scale. This role owns both.

The role sits at the intersection of product management and data science. You have the technical depth to build ML proof-of-concepts independently and the commercial judgment to translate those capabilities into products customers pay for. You write the strategy and the first notebook.

**What You'll Be Doing

****Define and own the data driven product strategy

**

• Own the roadmap for nShift's data intelligence layer: carrier performance prediction, cross-customer benchmarking, ML-driven carrier recommendations, and related capabilities.

• Translate nShift's data asset into a sequenced product strategy that delivers near-term value while building toward the compounding intelligence layer vision.

• Define the information architecture for the data insights layer: what data is collected, how it is normalized (in partnership with adjacent teams), and how it is exposed to upstream products.

• Make hard prioritization calls: what to build first to validate the ML hypothesis, what to defer, and what to kill when the data doesn't support the bet.

• Own the qualitative intelligence pipeline alongside the quantitative one: define which unstructured sources carry decision-relevant signal (support tickets, delivery exception messages, customer forum, carrier communications), how LLM-extracted insights are structured for downstream use, and how qualitative and quantitative signals combine into a coherent intelligence product.

• Own the positioning and differentiation narrative: why this dataset is uniquely nShift's, why no competitor can replicate it, and how to articulate that defensibility to enterprise buyers.

**Build and validate before engineering commits

**

• Run ML proof-of-concepts independently: data exploration, feature engineering, model selection, and initial validation, using Python, notebooks, and the data available in nShift's data layer.

• Define the evaluation framework for both ML models and LLM pipelines. For ML features: what accuracy thresholds matter, how to measure model performance in production, how to distinguish signal from noise. For LLM-based features: how to assess output consistency, factual grounding, and quality at scale, where traditional accuracy metrics don't apply.

• Design lightweight experiments that answer the key questions before a full engineering team is committed. Does the prediction accuracy justify the product? Does cross-customer data improve the model significantly? Is the data we have sufficient, or do we need to instrument more?

• Translate POC findings into clear build, kill, or iterate decisions backed by data.

**Partner across data, engineering, and commercial teams

**

• Work closely with engineers to define the data models, pipelines, and normalization standards needed to power ML features. You are a customer and co-designer of the data layer, not a passenger.

• Drive integration of data insights capabilities into existing products. Work closly with your PM peers to make this happen.

• Engage directly with customers and prospects across the full spectrum, from small shippers to global enterprises, to validate intelligence use cases: what decisions do they make today that better data would improve? What would they pay for? What do they trust?

• Build the commercial narrative: ROI frameworks, value quantification, and positioning for the target buyer.

**Govern the data responsibly

**

• Define the anonymization, aggregation, and consent frameworks that make cross-customer benchmarking legally and ethically sound, and credible to enterprise customers who will ask hard questions.

• Work with Legal and the DPO to ensure data usage within the intelligence layer meets GDPR and contractual obligations. The data asset is only valuable if customers trust nShift to use it appropriately.

• Establish transparency standards for ML-powered recommendations: when does a merchant see why a carrier was recommended? What level of explainability builds trust without revealing proprietary network data?

**What You'll Bring

****Must-have

**

• Hands-on data proficiency across both paradigms: you can build and validate ML proof-of-concepts (data exploration, feature engineering, model training, evaluation) using Python and standard ML tooling (scikit-learn, pandas, XGBoost, or equivalent), and you can design and evaluate LLM-based analysis pipelines (prompt design, retrieval-augmented approaches, output quality evaluation). You are not a data scientist or an ML engineer, but you can work like one when the problem requires it.

• Shipped ML-powered products: you have personally driven an ML or data intelligence product from initial hypothesis to production, including defining evaluation criteria, partnering with data engineers and scientists, and making commercial decisions based on model performance data.

• PM fundamentals with commercial depth: 3+ years shipping B2B SaaS products. You can build a business case, define pricing, run customer discovery, and hold direct conversations with enterprise buyers about ROI.

• Data literacy that earns engineering respect: you understand data models, pipeline design, normalization challenges, and the practical constraints of real production data. You can review a data schema and immediately ask the right questions.

• Clear communication across the technical and commercial boundary: you can explain a precision-recall tradeoff to a CPO and a carrier event data use case to a data engineer in the same afternoon, without condescending to either.

• Excellent written and verbal English: you will write strategy documents, ML experiment briefs, customer-facing product narratives, and present to leadership, often in the same week.

**Nice to have

**

• Experience with time-series or logistics domain data: carrier performance modelling, routing optimization, ETA prediction, or related domains.

• Familiarity with data platform concepts: data lake houses, feature stores, model registries, observability for ML in production.

• Background in cross-customer benchmarking or network intelligence products, where the value comes from aggregation rather than individual customer data.

• Experience with GDPR-compliant data product design in a multi-tenant B2B SaaS context.

• Nordic or European logistics market experience: carrier landscape, regulatory environment, freight economics.

• Track record of building the first data product at a company, defining standards rather than inheriting them.
